findings.title: Shared levels are downloaded and uploaded over cleartext HTTP
findings.code_excerpt:
public final static String USERLEVELS_GETPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoDice4k/get_level.php";
	public final static String USERLEVELS_SAVEPHP = "http://www.apo-games.de/apoDice4k/save_level.php";
findings.entry_point: The remote level response enters through ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.load() at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:153-182. Locally created level data enters the upload path through ApoDiceEditor.touchedButton()/uploadString() at ApoDiceEditor.java:138-158 and 185-188.
findings.sink: URLConnection transmits and receives without TLS in ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.save() at lines 121-137 and load() at lines 162-179.
findings.data_path: Startup calls ApoDicePanel.init() -> loadUserlevels() (ApoDicePanel.java:58-60,79-86) -> ApoDiceUserlevels.loadUserlevels() (ApoDiceUserlevels.java:22-30) -> ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.load() (lines 153-209). Upload follows ApoDiceEditor.uploadString() (ApoDiceEditor.java:185-188) -> ApoDiceUserlevels.addLevel() (ApoDiceUserlevels.java:83-89) -> ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.save() (lines 113-143).
findings.attack_scenario: On an attacker-controlled Wi-Fi network, the attacker intercepts the HTTP request to the endpoint defined at ApoDiceConstants.java:5. They replace the level feed with attacker-chosen, syntactically complete 11-line records. The client stores those strings at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:182-205 and exposes them as playable levels at ApoDiceUserlevels.java:27-32. The attacker can inject or censor shared content and can combine this with ApoDice-02 to crash the game. The same attacker can alter an outgoing level upload sent at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:130-133.
findings.preconditions: The device must report an active connection through ApoDice.isOnline() (ApoDice.java:48-52), the Android build/platform must permit cleartext traffic, and the attacker must control the server or the network path.
findings.validation_plan: In an authorized emulator, route www.apo-games.de through an intercepting proxy or test DNS mapping. Return a valid 11-line level record different from the legitimate response, launch the app, and tap userlevels. Seeing the injected level in the game and its plaintext request/response in the proxy proves the path. Repeat an editor upload and verify that the form body is readable and modifiable in transit.

findings.title: Downloaded level shorter than 64 characters crashes level loading
findings.entry_point: Every eleventh response line is accepted as a level string without length or alphabet validation at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:182-185.
findings.sink: ApoDicePuzzleGame.loadLevel() indexes all positions 0 through 63 with String.charAt() at line 187.
findings.data_path: ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.load() stores the response string (lines 182-185) -> ApoDiceUserlevels.getAllLevelsSorted() copies it into ApoDiceLevel.editorLevels (ApoDiceUserlevels.java:27-30,44-54) -> the userlevels button invokes ApoDicePanel.setPuzzleGame() (ApoDiceMenu.java:75-76; ApoDicePanel.java:136-146) -> loadLevel() selects editorLevels[p[1]] and calls charAt() (ApoDicePuzzleGame.java:176-187).
findings.attack_scenario: A malicious server or network attacker returns one complete 11-line record whose first line is just "0" and whose numeric metadata lines are valid. Loading succeeds and the userlevels button appears. When the victim taps it, charAt(0) succeeds but charAt(1) throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException at ApoDicePuzzleGame.java:187; no variant code catches the exception on this path, disrupting or crashing the game.
findings.preconditions: The attacker must cause the shared-level endpoint to return a short level string, either by controlling the service/content or by altering the cleartext response identified in ApoDice-01, and the victim must select userlevels.
findings.validation_plan: Serve an authorized test response containing these eleven fields in order: level "0", time 1.0, count 1, total 1, any name, four integer ratings, ID 1, and current time 1.0. Launch the app, wait for userlevels to become visible, and tap it. A logcat StringIndexOutOfBoundsException pointing to ApoDicePuzzleGame.loadLevel() line 187 confirms the issue.

findings.title: Unbounded level-feed response can exhaust application memory
findings.entry_point: A malicious level server or network attacker controls the response stream returned by urlConn.getInputStream() at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:179.
findings.sink: The EOF-controlled loop at lines 182-207 reads unbounded line lengths and appends an unbounded number of strings and boxed numeric values to eleven ArrayLists.
findings.data_path: ApoDicePanel.init() automatically starts loadUserlevels() at ApoDicePanel.java:58-60; its thread calls ApoDiceUserlevels.loadUserlevels() at lines 79-86, which calls ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.load() at ApoDiceUserlevels.java:22-25. The response then enters the unbounded read-and-append loop at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:179-207.
findings.attack_scenario: The attacker continuously sends valid 11-line records, or sends one extremely large first line, without closing the response. Because neither line length nor record count is capped at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:182-207, heap usage grows until the Android process raises OutOfMemoryError and terminates. This load begins automatically rather than requiring a level-selection tap.
findings.preconditions: The app must be online, cleartext traffic must be permitted, and the attacker must control the endpoint or HTTP response path long enough to stream the payload.
findings.validation_plan: In a test emulator with a constrained heap, redirect the endpoint to a lab server that streams repeated valid 11-line records indefinitely. Launch the app and monitor `adb shell dumpsys meminfo` and logcat. Monotonically growing heap followed by OutOfMemoryError originating from readLine or the ArrayList additions confirms the weakness.

findings.title: Editable SharedPreferences value unlocks every built-in level
findings.entry_point: A local user with access to the app-private preferences file can modify the `solved` integer in ApoDicePref, whose name is defined at ApoDiceConstants.java:11 and opened at ApoDice.java:43.
findings.sink: ApoDicePuzzleChooser.setSolved() trusts the stored value and clamps it only to MAX_LEVELS-1 at lines 66-74; touchedPressed() then permits every index less than or equal to that value at lines 83-87.
findings.data_path: ApoDice.onCreate() opens the preferences (ApoDice.java:43) -> ApoDicePanel.init() calls loadPreferences() (ApoDicePanel.java:64) -> getInt() supplies the edited value (lines 67-69) -> solvedLevel() forwards it to ApoDicePuzzleChooser.setSolved() (ApoDicePanel.java:179-180; ApoDicePuzzleChooser.java:66-77) -> the chooser authorizes level selection using i <= solved (ApoDicePuzzleChooser.java:83-87).
findings.attack_scenario: On a rooted emulator/device or an accessible debug installation, the user edits ApoDicePref.xml and sets `solved` to 2147483647. On relaunch, setSolved() clamps it to MAX_LEVELS-1 at ApoDicePuzzleChooser.java:69-70, and the i <= solved check at lines 84-86 makes every built-in level selectable. The gain is progression cheating only.
findings.preconditions: The attacker needs local access to app-private storage, such as root, emulator access, or a build permitting `run-as`/backup access. The supplied generated BuildConfig declares DEBUG=true at gen/net/apogames/apodice/BuildConfig.java:5, but the Android manifest is not present to independently verify debuggability.
findings.validation_plan: Install the variant on a rooted test emulator, launch it once, force-stop it, and change the `solved` integer in shared_prefs/ApoDicePref.xml to 2147483647. Relaunch, open the puzzle chooser, and select the final built-in level without completing predecessors. Successful selection confirms the trust bypass.

notes: The supplied root contains 19 handwritten Java source files and two generated Java files, but no Android manifest, build configuration, resources, server implementation, or BitsEngine dependency source. Consequently, platform cleartext policy and dependency-level exception handling cannot be verified. No ClassLoader/defineClass, ObjectInputStream, filesystem path construction, MessageDigest, JNI load, Applet, credential, or secret API appears in the reviewed files. The editor exposes Upload after the local solver succeeds at ApoDiceEditor.java:159-175, while save() sends only the level at ApoDiceUserlevelsLoad.java:113-143; because the server implementation is absent, this audit does not assume that the server omits independent validation and does not count that as a separate finding.
